subject: Private deployment: maintenance contract, safety lanes, and rollback acceptance
messages:
From: Tom Gallagher <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@medicore.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Planned private maintenance window & rollback questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're lining up a maintenance window for the private deployment (VPC) pilot and want to confirm the safe path for the upgrade: version pin removal, rollout cadence, and abort/rollback triggers. Key asks from our side: 

- Final list of exact binaries/versions that will be pushed and the fallback images kept on standby.
- Network-level steps: expected BGP quiesce, NAT/GW changes, and timing for connection drain.
- Acceptance criteria for the canary phase and who signs off (Acme ops vs. Redwood SRE).
- Explicit SLA/credit implications if the upgrade causes significant service degradation.

We'd also like to run a formal dry-run in our staging VPC next week (canary with 3% traffic) and capture a play-by-play for our auditors. Attached is our high-level calendar and an initial risk matrix.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will keep the previous version pinned for at least 48 hours after the rollout completes, and the exact procedure to shelve/unpin in an emergency?

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Director — Acme Health
Attachment: acme_maintenance_calendar.csv (text/csv)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Gallagher <ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned private maintenance window & rollback questions

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. Summarizing answers and next steps so we have a single reference for the audit: 

1) Version artifacts and fallback policy
- Planned push: redwood-inference-serve v1.9.2 (quantized x64 build) to private fleet.
- Fallback images: v1.9.1 and v1.8.7 will be pre-staged on the control plane and kept on each node's image cache for 72 hours post-rollout.
- Emergency unpin: our control-plane endpoint exposes a single-button "shelve-version" that triggers a forced drain and reattach to the pre-staged image; expected recovery time 8–12 minutes under typical load.

2) Network steps (ops summary)
- Preflight (T-72h): verify BGP sessions, route reflectors, and NAT health; capture baseline flow logs.
- Dry-run (staging): 3% canary for 4 hours with traffic mirroring to a shadow pool.
- Cutover (production window): incremental node-by-node restart with KV cache warmup; expected per-node impact ~45–90s.
- Cordon/uncordon operations are automated via the orchestration plane; manual network rollback requires our NOC to withdraw new routes at the edge — we will coordinate with your netops.

3) Acceptance criteria and signoff
- Canary fine-grain: no increase >2x in 95th percentile latency and <0.5% error-rate bump for 30m sliding window.
- Telemetry: token-level latency traces and model-level failure counters will be published in the shared dashboard.
- Signoff: Acme will provide a single-statement approval in the shared doc; Redwood SRE will mark the rollout green in the console.

4) SLA/credits
- For this pilot we will honor our standard maintenance policy (no SLA credits for scheduled windows) but will consider an exception if an unplanned platform regression causes >30m of sustained outage attributable to the release. We'll enumerate the exact credit calculation in the maintenance addendum.

Next actions: 
- Karthik & Neha, can you confirm the exact shelf/unpin API call id and whether we can provide a pre-signed runbook for Acme's NOC?
- Tom, can your team confirm a dry-run slot (we're proposing Aug 23 02:00–06:00 UTC) and who will be the on-call signatory?

I've attached an internal risk matrix (redwood_private_maintenance_risk_matrix.xlsx) and will add the dry-run logs after the rehearsal.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_private_maintenance_risk_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Tom Gallagher <ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned private maintenance window & rollback questions

All — quick operational notes from SRE side after the dry-run this morning (we did the 3% canary in staging, captured mop-dryrun-log-20260823.txt):

- Dry-run outcome: canary passed acceptance thresholds; 95th latency increase ~1.3x during cache warmup, error-rate unchanged. Telemetry captured in the shared dashboard link.
- Shelve/unpin API: POST /internal/v1/pinning/shelve 
  payload: {"fleet_id":"<redwood-fleet>","target_version":"v1.9.1","reason":"emergency-shelve"} — we'll provide a pre-signed curl snippet in the runbook. (We'll attach the snippet to the drive folder.)
- Rollback ladder (recommended): 1) Initiate shelve (forced drain), 2) Withdraw the new BGP announcements at edge if connectivity remains impacted, 3) Trigger fleet-wide revert to v1.9.1, 4) Validate KV cache consistency via the consistency-check endpoint.
- Rollback timing: best-case 8–12 minutes; allowed worst-case 25 minutes if we need to rehydrate caches from cold storage. Plan for a 30-minute maintenance window cushion per tranche.
- Comms: Jonas will coordinate the on-call paging and call bridge. Acme: please confirm the on-call signatory and whether Medicore (Marta) should be on the bridge for audit purposes.

I'll upload the pre-signed runbook and the exact curl example to the Drive folder by EOD. If anyone needs a short runthrough, happy to schedule a 30-minute ops dry-run tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, SRE — Redwood Inference
Attachment: mop-dryrun-log-20260823.txt (text/plain)
